a:r.a:t: Yeast are the simplest eukaryote for DNA recombination.
They have linear chromosomes with telomere ends, which can be unstable in vitro.
YAC is circular to accommodate quick replication and stable storage but has a removable segment that linearizes the product for transformation.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the process of the construction of a yeast artificial chromosome using vectors. At the top of the diagram is a large vector, which is a ring with multicolored bands. It is labeled “YAC vector” in the middle. The majority of the vector is tan, with the topmost long tan section labeled EcoRI in pink, to the upper right. The next vector is a light blue segment labeled selectable marker Y; below this is another tan section. Below this is a short red section with a pointed left end labeled TEL; the pointed end is labeled BamHI in pink. To the left of this is another long tan section, with another TEL section with its pointed end to the right and labeled BamHI. Above this is another tan section, then a short light blue section labeled selectable marker X. To the upper right of this is a short tan section, then a short dark tan section labeled ori. To the immediate right is a short yellow section labeled CEN which completes the circle. Below this is a down arrow with a divergent arrow pointing left to a large tan segment, indicating its removal. To the right of the arrow is a gray text box reading, “BamHI digestion creates linear chromosome with telomeric ends.” Below this arrow is the YAC vector stretched out into a straight flat line. The red TEL sections are on either end. To the right of the left TEL section is a tan section, then the X section, then a short tan section, then a dark tan Ori section, then the yellow CEN section, then a long tan EcoRI section, then the light blue Y section, then a short tan section, then the short red TEL section at the end. Below this is a down arrow with a text box to the right with text reading, “EcoRI digestion creates two arms, each with a selectable marker (X or Y).” The below image shows that the middle part of the tan EcoRI section has been removed, so there are now two “arms” of the vector. Below this is a down arrow with a convergent arrow showing the addition of short, curled orange segments labeled “ligate.” A gray text box to the right reads, “Fragments of genomic DNA generated by incomplete digestion with EcoRI.” Below this arrow is an image of the straightened vector, but the two arms have been connected by an orange strip made of the ligate. The picture is labeled YAC below. Below is a down arrow labeled “transform.” Below is a sequence of yeast cells, which are round and yellow, with a light brown outline representing the cell wall. The cell to the left is labeled “yeast cell” and has a white portion circle in the center full of blue genetic material, shown as short wavy blue lines. To the right is an arrow labeled, “digest cell wall enzymatically” above. To the right is an image of the cell without the cell wall, as simply a yellow circle containing blue genetic material labeled “yeast spheroplast.” To the right is an arrow labeled “select for X and Y above.” To the right of this is a yeast cell with the cell wall around it. Among the blue genetic material is a single red fragment. It is labeled, “Yeast with YAC clone.”
